title: Securities (Amendment) Act 2004

(3) A foreign broker dealer or limited service broker
licensed by the Commission may become a member of a securities
exchange provided it meets the securities exchange’s requirements for
membership as set out in its rules.
(4) An investment adviser that is licensed by the Commission must be
licensed by the Commission as an investment adviser under sections 54
and 55, but only if he conducts business or holds himself out as

conducting business in a member territory.
(5) A principal of, a foreign broker dealer or limited
service broker that is licensed by the Commission, must be licensed by the
Commission as a principal under sections 60 and 61, but only if he
conducts business or holds himself out as conducting business in a
member territory.
(6) A representative of, a foreign broker dealer or limited
service broker that is licensed by the Commission, must be licensed by the
Commission as a representative under sections 62, 63 and 64, but only if
he conducts business or holds himself out as conducting business in a
member territory.
(7) The term “conducting business, or holds himself out as
conducting business” as used in subsections (4, 5 and 6) shall include but
not be limited to
(a) use of the telephone, telegraph, mails,
Internet, e-mail or any other means to
communicate with investors or potential
investors located in a member territory,
whether on a regular or sporadic basis;
(b) visiting investors or potential investors in a
member territory, whether singly or in
groups, to communicate with them about an
investment in securities, whether on a
regular or sporadic basis; or
(c) registration as a principal or representative
with a securities exchange in connection

service broker’s membership in a securities
exchange;

combination of activities described in
(i) section 47 in the case of foreign

brokers, or

investment advisers,

or activities takes place in a

communicate with the

(8) A person is subject to the requirements of
subsections (4), (5) and (6) if he participates in any of the activities listed
in subsection (7) even if he is not physically present in a member territory
when he participates in the activity.
